subPhases.title: Anchors, insets, vertical text
subPhases.result: every `ST_TextVerticalType` draws: the WordArt cell is seven sixths of the font box and square, exact on 7 of 9 faces, so the corpus scores 155 of 155 slides with none refused. Two bugs the fixtures had been catching unread: the insets did not turn with the frame, and `mongolianVert` stacked its columns in reverse

subPhases.title: Fidelity harness
subPhases.result: the gate had been reporting PASS over 155 slides while gating 152, because a slide the baseline had never heard of counted as unchanged; it now refuses to score one it holds no digest for, and `--record` needs a written reason and the exact count it will move. Every differing cell is charged to the shape that painted it, which found a third bad shape on `a03-fills-02` that two passes over its heatmap had missed and put numbers on two of 2.7's recorded open questions. The clock a slide draws moves 31 cells at maxD 6, an order of magnitude under the rasteriser's own noise. The Linux baseline is recorded and CI runs the gate, which caught two breaks a Windows-only run never could: the workflow had ordered Build after Lint, so `check` had been red on every push to main, a committed README linked to a gitignored file, and three of 3.7 font tests asserted what this machine has rather than what the code does

subPhases.title: First npm release: `render-svg` and `cli render`
subPhases.result: the plan called this a release and it was really a measurement: `render-svg` was already a pure string function that ran in Node, but text needed a canvas and there is none, so `pptx-studio render` reads the font own tables instead. That is a second measurement engine, and no real font can say what the first one does - Arial `hhea.ascender` and its `OS/2.usWinAscent` are both 1854 - so T13 built seven fonts that disagree with themselves on purpose and asked Chromium. The face box is `usWin`, or `sTypo` where `fsSelection` bit 7 is set (14/14, against 10/14 for `hhea`, which is what everybody writes first); pair kerning is GPOS where the font has a `kern` feature and the legacy table otherwise (42/42, against 36/42 for preferring the legacy one, which is the cheaper parse and wrong on every font carrying both); a width is each advance truncated and each kern rounded at 1/65536 px (252/252, against 88/252 for exact floats). The advance is linear in size to within 1.04e-4 px, which is the finding the whole approach rests on: the browser does not hint it. The reader reproduces all 252 widths exactly and 19 of 19 mutants die. Running the release path found that changesets/action renamed its four inputs, so Release had been red on every push to main since 0.1, and that no package carried a LICENSE or a NOTICE, which Apache-2.0 4(a) and 4(d) require and ours is not decorative - it carries POI attribution for the 187 presets
subPhases.note: all eleven packages are on npm at 0.1.0 with provenance. A trusted publisher cannot be attached to a package that does not exist, so the first publish went out from a one-time token job that has since been deleted. Releases are dispatched by hand from the Actions tab now: there is no version pull request, so the repository does not need "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests", which is a single toggle covering both verbs. No PNG - rasterising means shipping a rasteriser, and the point of the verb is that it needs nothing but Node. No shaping, so Arabic and Devanagari measure wide
